themes_detail.label: Homeless outreach surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless Person Assistance complaints spiked to 10 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 471% increase—suggesting either a concentration of unhoused individuals or a failure of existing outreach services in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 10 Homeless Person Assistance complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (471% spike, z-score: 5.03)
Recurring budget request for 'outreach services to homebound older adults' suggests chronic underinvestment in vulnerable populations
High-density student and institutional presence (Columbia University, hospitals) may strain social services
reporting_angles: Are city-contracted outreach teams adequately staffed in this district? Interview Department of Social Services and local nonprofits.
Where are unhoused individuals congregating and why? Map 311 complaints against shelter capacity and street counts.

themes_detail.label: Water quality deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Water Quality complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.2 per-week average—a 1100% spike—raising questions about water system integrity or contamination events affecting the district.
evidence: 3 Water Quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Heat/Hot Water complaints remain extremely high at 4140 over 90 days, suggesting aging infrastructure stress
Water Leak complaints (376 total) and Plumbing complaints (726 total) indicate potential systemic distribution issues
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to request water testing results and recent main breaks in the district.
Interview residents in affected buildings; cross-reference complaints by address to identify clustered contamination.

themes_detail.label: Street lighting emergency
themes_detail.summary: Street Light Condition complaints surged to 29 LAST WEEK, up 404% from a 5.8 per-week baseline (z-score: 7.78), creating public safety hazards and indicating backlog in DOT maintenance across the district.
evidence: 29 Street Light Condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.8 weekly baseline (404% spike, z-score: 7.78)
Recurring budget request for 'Other capital request (DOT)' suggests unfunded maintenance backlog
Spike is recent but not this-week—slightly lower recency than water or homeless issues
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with DOT for street light repair requests and timeline in CD 109; identify which neighborhoods are darkest.
Interview Community Board about maintenance backlog; connect safety concerns (mugging, accidents) to lighting gaps.

themes_detail.label: Food poisoning cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food Poisoning complaints hit 3 LAST WEEK versus 0.1 per-week historical average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—warranting swift investigation into restaurant or food vendor contamination in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 3 Food Poisoning complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
District is home to Columbia University and hospitals with high foot traffic; student population vulnerable to foodborne illness
No follow-up complaints this week—may indicate isolated incident or end of exposure
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to identify which facilities generated complaints and inspection status.
Interview affected individuals and Columbia student health services to understand scope and source of outbreak.

themes_detail.label: Park rule violations spike
themes_detail.summary: Violation of Park Rules complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.1 per-week average—a 2300% spike—suggesting either enforcement crackdowns or deteriorating park conditions and community conflict in district green spaces.
evidence: 3 Violation of Park Rules complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Recurring budget request for 'Reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' indicates aging infrastructure and possible maintenance neglect
Small absolute numbers limit confidence; may reflect data error or single enforcement event rather than systemic issue
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to clarify what violations were reported—enforcement sweep, or genuine rule-breaking uptick?
Visit parks in district (Morningside Park, St. Nicholas Park) to observe conditions and interview park-goers about conflicts.
